message.content:
In Ancient Greece the authority to **establish laws and orders** lay in a few key offices and individuals: | Office / Person | Role in law‑making | Greek term | |-----------------|-------------------|------------| | **Archons** (chief magistrates) | Each city‑state elected a set of archons who had the power to enact new laws and oversee their enforcement. | ἀρχόντες (archontes) | | **Ekklesia** (assembly) | The popular assembly could approve or reject laws proposed by the council or magistrates. | ἐκκλησία (ekklesia) | | **Boule** (council of 500) | The council drafted legislation and presented it to the assembly. | βουλή (boule) | | **Lawgivers** | Certain individuals were celebrated for codifying major legal reforms. | νομογένεστος (nomogenestos) – “lawgiver” | | **Notable lawgivers** | • **Draco** – first to write a written code in Athens (c. 620 BCE).
• **Solon** – reformed Athenian law and politics (c. 594 BCE).
• **Lycurgus** – reformed Spartan society (c. 6th century BCE). | νομογένεστος (nomogenestos) | ### Greek words you’ll find useful | English | Greek | Transliteration | |---------|-------|-----------------| | law | νόμος | nomos | | order | τάξις | taxis | | lawgiver / lawmaker | νόμογένεστος | nomogenestos | | to establish / institute | θεσπίζω | thespizō | | to legislate | νομιζέω | nomizēō | ### How to say the question in Greek > **Ποιος θεσπίζει νόμους και τάξεις;** > *Poios thespizēi nomous kai taxis?* This literally asks, “Who establishes laws and orders?” and captures the idea of the law‑making authority in Ancient Greek society.
